releases.notes:
# CCC 1.1.2

CCC now ignores unrelated or unchanged RCP camera status messages and publishes
workspace snapshots and connection status only when their values change. This
removes redundant background updates while preserving fresh recording reports
needed to confirm recording commands.

- Adds camera-specific selection feedback for Enable / Disable Camera, including
  when a selected camera or its RCP is offline.
- Keeps the CCC workspace module Ready when local camera selection is available;
  individual camera rows continue to report connection problems.
- Uses Enable / Disable Camera, Enable / Disable All Cameras, Start Recording,
  Stop Recording, and Toggle Recording as the action names. Existing action IDs,
  camera selections, and saved settings remain compatible.

## Qualification

- All 44 CCC tests across six files passed, including repeated recording reports,
  unchanged notification suppression, offline selection feedback, and recording
  coordination.
- TypeScript, module build, conformance, and packaging checks passed.
- The release archive rebuilds byte for byte from the reviewed source and matches
  the locally installed 1.1.2 package.
- Live service logs recorded 17 successful Stream Deck executions after the
  local update, with a median service execution time of 27 ms. Physical button
  display latency was not independently measured.

Beta of the Cyanview configuration module (`lightlab-cyanview-config`) with the work done since 0.1.36.

- Camera Configuration is one list of every camera, with a Source for each. Changing a camera's Source moves it to that controller.

- Devices is one sheet with a row for each controller, including its name and LAN addresses.
- Button presses go to a controller over MQTT alone. It is tried on its base address first, then on the address it was added by.
- A send opens only the controllers it changes, and a controller's edits go together.
- A rig that was set up outside the module is read in after Refresh all, and a Review asks whether to keep or clear what Hubble did not configure.
- The page is tidier: a camera count, Hubble's own lists, Add and Add all for found devices, Clear all cameras, and Command-Plus and Command-Minus for sheet text size.
- A Tilta iris has a Direction cell, Normal or Swapped, and sends that fail are written to Hubble's log.

Requires Hubble 2.0.18 or later.

releases.notes:
Cyanview configuration (`lightlab-cyanview-config`) 0.1.62, the first Stable release since 0.1.36. It brings everything from the 0.1.50 and 0.1.52 betas plus the work since.

- Camera Configuration is one list of every camera, with a Source for each, and REMI Matrix attaches a camera to other RCPs. Any change to a camera rebuilds its REMI copies, and what an RCP leaves behind is deleted.
- Devices, Pending sends, faster sends that open only the controllers a change involves, and a Review for rigs set up outside the module.
- Changes made on a Cyanview controller show up as they happen.
- Camera Enabled On and Off, with a refresh, and REMI copies follow their source camera.
- Button Matrix feedback: recording, state and connection light keys through module triggers, each action with its own triggers. Select camera lights as soon as the controller acknowledges, and camera keys show Online only when the camera itself is online.
- Record camera starts on a tap and stops only on a two-second hold, blinking green until it has stopped.
- A Tilta iris Direction cell, the Cyanview sidebar logo, and a tidier page.

Requires Hubble 2.2.0 or later, for module feedback triggers and held presses. Older Hubble builds list this release as unsupported and keep their current version.

Tested against simulated devices, in a packaged Hubble 2.2.0 on isolated ports, and these exact bytes have run in a production Hubble workspace since November 13. Not yet run on physical Cyanview controllers.

VENICE Camera Control (`venice-camera-control`) 0.1.27, its first catalog release. A full-page spreadsheet for Sony VENICE 2 cameras: one row per camera, 265 settings in 11 groups, with Refresh, Send, Manual or Auto send, Pending sends, a Live switch that follows changes made at the camera, a Recording column and optional alerts when a camera drops.

- Recording now reads REC from the card's recording report, since the media box reports NoMedia while rolling.

Username and Password are saved in the workspace, so they appear as plain text in workspace exports and support logs.

Requires Hubble 2.1.1 or later, for module-owned alerts. Reads, Live, Recording and the reel number have been used on real VENICE 2 cameras with 0.1.26; these 0.1.27 bytes have been tested against a loopback camera simulator and loaded in a packaged Hubble 2.2.0 on isolated ports, not on a real camera. Writes to settings other than Camera ID, reel number and SDI 3/4 Info have not been confirmed on a camera.
